field_plants.note: Field prefab root (the wiki building) -> the plant prefab it grows and its planting spots

plants.classes: WorkspotBehaviour + FormulaStepBehaviour on the plant (harvest or felling, WorkIterations = work actions) and SpawnerBehaviour children (one prefab per spawn event; spawn_yield is what harvesting that prefab gives)

biomes.note: Sandbox configuration per biome: what the player may place and what the map generator scatters (density per tile). Campaign levels list their own buildable entries. Asset GUIDs resolved through each prefab root SerializedKey.

eating.note: Priority of the eat activity against everything else a villager could do, by the status of the need the item would satisfy. Full means never. Identical on every villager prefab.

salvage.note: Only objects with an OverrideRecycleValue are listed (ruins, expedition crates, gifts, canoes, pallets, planter build sites). The other 280 recyclable objects store no amounts; their refund is computed in code.

Decorative Planter Calla Lilly Build Site

workspot_effects.note: Only five workspots in the game carry either behaviour.

level_event_schedule.note: Per packaged level, each placed event prefab with the game day it starts (DaysStart). Villager and resource spawns come from the prefab; ambient events (birds, fireflies, seasonal decoration) carry no spawn. announced_days_before is how long before the day the game shows its notice; 1000 means from the start of the level, 0 means no notice.

social_spots.note: Units a villager gains from one use of a spot, the use duration (raw units, not days), and whether the spot can be picked to satisfy Community or Fun. Roots that are not buildings (for example ParkSocialSpots, OpenKitchenEatSpot) are nested spot prefabs that buildings instantiate. Duration units and the per-use versus per-day question are unverified.

duplicate_resource_names.note: 284895 is the GameObject "FakeStick" under the Firewood Yard (Woodchopper): 1 Log becomes 4 FakeStick, then FakeStick becomes Stick 1:1. It shares the localization key Resource.Stick, so both display as Stick.

day_night_cycle.note: The curve maps cycle progress to a keyframe index 0..4 (Night, Sunrise, Day, Sunset, back to Night); the tournament curve is non-linear. How cycle progress aligns with the work-time fractions is not stored here.

ui_style.note: Colours as the game stores them. Each category names the palette entry its icon background uses and the frame drawn around the icon; building lists are prefab roots in build-menu order. Frame sprites are texture sprites (background tinted with the category colour, lines in the Text colour) with the icon placed inside the anchor box.
